claim: Generally true to size; deviations noted on product pages
exact_words: Our shoes generally run true to size and align with standard industry sizing. If a style runs smaller or larger, we note that on the product page to help you choose the best size.

claim: Printable measuring tools for size and width
exact_words: Download and print our sizing tools for men, women and kids to easily find your shoe size. These printable measuring charts help you find your size and width and offer tips for finding your best fit.

claim: Choose the larger size between sizes
exact_words: Choose the larger size if your feet are between sizes. You can adjust for a better fit with socks, insoles and lacing patterns.

claim: Try on late afternoon
exact_words: Try shoes on in the late afternoon when your feet are at their largest due to normal swelling.

claim: Toe room to wiggle
exact_words: You should have enough room in the toe box to wiggle your toes.

claim: Fit the larger foot
exact_words: Be sure to try shoes on both feet. Your left and right feet may differ in length or width as much as a full size. Always buy shoes that fit your larger foot.

claim: Too-small purchases more common
exact_words: People are more than twice as likely to buy a shoe that is too small than too big.

exact_words: Measure the distance between the marks. Taking the larger of the two measurements, use the conversion chart to find your correct shoe size.

claim: True Fit without measuring (Get Started / Sign In)

claim: Measure at end of day
exact_words: Follow these easy steps to get the right size. For the best fit, measure your feet at the end of the day.

claim: Length: big toe tip to outermost heel
exact_words: 1. Length: Measure the distance from the tip of your big toe to the outermost part of your heel.

claim: Chart follows standard sizing
exact_words: The adidas shoe size chart for men follows standard sizing. The shoe size chart should therefore reflect your normal fit but check the information on this page for more details.

claim: Measure in usual socks
exact_words: Before measuring, put on the socks you typically wear with your shoes.

claim: Big toe to outermost heel is the foot's length
exact_words: After tracing your foot, use your ruler to measure the distance between your big toe and the outermost part of your heel to learn the length of your foot.

claim: Walking shoes: a thumb's width
exact_words: aim for walking shoes with a thumb’s width between your longest toe and the front of the shoe.

claim: Running shoes: half a thumb's width
exact_words: There should be half a thumb’s width of space at the front of your running shoe.

claim: Up a half or full size for exercise
exact_words: Keep in mind, feet tend to swell when you're active, so if you know you’ll be wearing the shoe while exercising, consider going up a half or even full size.

claim: Width standard at US men's 9
exact_words: In U.S. men’s sizing, if your foot width is about 4.2 inches at size 9, that’s standard; if it’s more than 4.4 inches, you’re in wide territory.

claim: UK blog: up a half or full size for exercise

claim: UK blog: same measuring steps, in trainers' socks

claim: US: measure at the end of the day
exact_words: Follow these steps to determine your shoe size. Do this during or at the end of the day for accuracy, as feet swell throughout the day.

claim: US: heel against a wall, mark longest toe and heel
exact_words: Place a piece of paper under your foot. Stand up straight and have your heel lightly touching against a wall. Mark the tip of your longest toe and heel on the paper. Measure the length of your feet from heel to toe.

claim: US: compare the measurement with the chart directly (no allowance stated)
exact_words: Repeat the steps for your other foot and compare the measurements with our size chart below.

claim: US: running shoes a half size up from casual
exact_words: For running shoes, we generally recommend sizing up a half size from your casual shoe size.

claim: Two footbed widths
